group.description: The `expects` vocabulary: what an asset needs from its host rather than from a named dependency. A port satisfied by the template's `provides` block is not copied into an adoption closure, which is what keeps deep layering affordable under copy-adoption.

capabilities.title: Design tokens
capabilities.description: The semantic and component token layers an asset styles against, exposed as runtime custom properties so a theme change does not re-render the tree.

port.contract: Supplies the active kit's primitive ramps, semantic tokens, and component tokens as runtime custom properties, and switches them coherently on theme or density change.

capabilities.rationale: The foundational port. Template-seeded per the foundations decision, so no adoption ever copies tokens; an asset requiring a newer token version than the target provides is a blocking finding rather than a silent copy.

capabilities.title: UI composition root
capabilities.description: The single boundary that composes theme, locale, direction, motion policy, density, portal host, interaction modality, and global managers.

port.contract: Mounts once at the application root and supplies theme, locale, direction, motion policy, density, portal host, and interaction modality to every descendant through one stable boundary.

capabilities.rationale: Its absence is the single highest-value adoption-scanner finding: a scenario missing the provider will have components that appear to work and silently lose theming, direction, and motion policy.

capabilities.title: Router adapter
capabilities.description: The seam through which links, navigation blocking, route state, scroll restoration, and transition direction reach the consuming scenario's router.

port.contract: Supplies current route state, performs navigation, registers navigation blockers for unsaved work, and reports history direction so transitions and scroll restoration can be correct.

capabilities.rationale: Required by every page template. Expressing route behavior as a port rather than an import is what keeps templates valid for the native targets, where there is no react-router at all.

capabilities.title: Typed data source
capabilities.description: The seam through which a template or collection receives its data, its loading and error conditions, and its refresh and pagination operations — without the library ever fetching domain data itself.

port.contract: Supplies typed records plus their loading, empty, partial, error, stale, and offline conditions, and accepts refresh, pagination, and cancellation requests bound to an AbortSignal.

capabilities.rationale: The port that makes page templates independently validatable: a fixture can satisfy it, so a template's loading, empty, partial, and error states can be captured in the catalog with no scenario adopting it. Parameterized because an untyped data source cannot be checked against a fixture's shape.

capabilities.title: Validation adapter
capabilities.description: The seam that normalizes schema validation, server-returned field errors, and async validation into one issue format the form runtime understands.

port.contract: Validates a value against a supplied schema and normalizes results, including server-returned errors, into one issue format carrying field path, message, and severity.

capabilities.title: Localization adapter
capabilities.description: The seam supplying translated strings, pluralization, number and date formatting, writing direction, and locale switching.

port.contract: Resolves message keys with interpolation and pluralization, formats numbers and dates for the active locale, and reports writing direction so layout and gestures can adapt.

capabilities.rationale: Direction reporting is the part components actually depend on — without it the RTL half of the locale axis cannot be satisfied even once the axis is wired.

capabilities.title: Icon registry
capabilities.description: The seam resolving icon names to renderable geometry with normalized optical sizing, stroke policy, direction awareness, and accessibility metadata.

port.contract: Resolves an icon name to renderable geometry with normalized optical size and stroke weight, flips directional icons for RTL, and carries whether an icon is decorative or meaningful.

capabilities.rationale: A registry rather than direct imports is what makes icon-weight-consistency checkable at all, and it is the seam that keeps a broad icon-package import out of the bundle.

capabilities.title: Layer manager
capabilities.description: The single coordinator for portals, stacking order, modal isolation, nested overlays, inert background content, and scroll locking.

port.contract: Assigns stacking order from the declared layer ramp, marks background content inert while a modal layer is open, reference-counts scroll locks, and orders dismissal so escape closes only the topmost eligible surface.

capabilities.rationale: Every overlay capability depends on it. Two independent layer managers in one application is the defect that produces dialogs behind backdrops, and it is detectable by the adoption scanner.

capabilities.title: Live announcer
capabilities.description: The single announcement service used by forms, drag operations, navigation, loading states, and async results.

port.contract: Queues, deduplicates, and times polite and assertive announcements through one live region, so competing regions never talk over each other.

capabilities.rationale: Required by status-announced. Multiple live regions is worse than none — screen readers interleave them unpredictably — so this must be a single host-provided service rather than a per-component concern.

capabilities.title: Preference storage adapter
capabilities.description: The seam persisting UI preferences, panel sizes, drafts, and layout state, with versioning and cross-tab coordination.

port.contract: Reads and writes versioned preference values through a pluggable backend, migrates stored values on version change, and synchronizes across tabs without clobbering concurrent writes.

capabilities.title: Telemetry adapter
capabilities.description: The seam receiving normalized UI outcome events, and a no-op when telemetry is disabled.

port.contract: Receives normalized UI outcome events carrying no user-supplied values, and behaves as a no-op when telemetry is unavailable or disabled.

capabilities.rationale: Explicitly value-free: the contract is that components report that a validation failed, never what was typed.

capabilities.title: Upload adapter
capabilities.description: The seam connecting file fields and upload flows to a concrete transfer implementation.

port.contract: Accepts files with progress reporting, cancellation, and retry, and reports terminal success or failure per file rather than per batch.

capabilities.title: Permissions adapter
capabilities.description: The seam through which feature and authorization gates resolve, so components never learn about domain roles.

port.contract: Answers whether a named capability is permitted, unavailable, or undetermined for the current actor, without exposing role or policy detail to the requesting component.

capabilities.rationale: Keeps permission-explained satisfiable without any component knowing what a role is — the gate asks about a capability, not about who the user is.

capabilities.title: Positioning adapter
capabilities.description: The seam through which anchored surfaces compute placement, collision handling, flipping, shifting, and arrow position, without exposing the positioning engine's types across component APIs.

port.contract: Positions a floating element relative to an anchor with collision detection, axis flipping, shifting, and arrow placement, and reports the resolved side so components can orient their transition origin.

capabilities.title: Virtualization adapter
capabilities.description: The seam connecting large lists, grids, calendars, logs, and option collections to a windowing implementation through stable measurement and focus interfaces.

port.contract: Windows a large collection with dynamic item measurement and overscan, and preserves keyboard focus and scroll anchoring across window changes so virtualization is never observable as lost focus.

capabilities.title: Date and time adapter
capabilities.description: The seam supplying date parsing, formatting, arithmetic, calendar systems, and timezone resolution to every temporal field and surface.

port.contract: Parses and formats dates and times for the active locale and calendar system, performs timezone-aware arithmetic, and reports week start and era conventions.

capabilities.title: Editor adapter
capabilities.description: The seam connecting rich text, Markdown, code, and JSON fields to lazily loaded editor implementations behind one value and validation contract.

port.contract: Mounts a lazily loaded editor for a declared content kind and exchanges value, selection, and validation state through one contract regardless of the underlying implementation.

capabilities.title: Charts adapter
capabilities.description: The seam connecting the chart framework to one or more rendering engines while keeping theme, data contracts, interaction, and accessibility consistent.

port.contract: Renders a declared chart specification through a pluggable engine, resolving scales and marks from theme tokens and exposing an accessible textual equivalent of the plotted data.

capabilities.title: Drag and drop adapter
capabilities.description: The seam connecting sortable and drag interactions to an implementation while preserving the library's selection, announcement, and drop contracts.

port.contract: Tracks an active drag with collision resolution against registered drop targets, and emits the position announcements that keyboard-accessible dragging depends on.

capabilities.title: Motion adapter
capabilities.description: The seam connecting motion primitives to the selected animation implementation while preserving the kit's declared transition classes and reduced-motion policy.

port.contract: Executes a declared transition class against an element and reports its measured duration, so motion tokens remain the source of truth regardless of the animation engine underneath.

capabilities.title: Platform feedback adapter
capabilities.description: The seam connecting optional haptic, sound, clipboard, share, and native-shell behaviors to whatever the running platform actually offers.

port.contract: Reports which platform feedback channels are available and performs those that are, degrading silently to no-ops rather than failing when a channel is unsupported.

capabilities.rationale: Kept optional by construction: a component that hard-depends on haptics is broken on every device without them, so availability reporting is part of the contract rather than an afterthought.
